Title: Explore and analyse models
Link: https://docs.solidatus.com/solidatus-6.5/models/explore-and-analyse-models
Content: Many people using Solidatus will spend their time browsing, exploring, and analysing models that have already been created and updated by others.

Models are analytical tools, and these pages are meant to cover model functionality that goes beyond putting things into them.

Analysing a model can take several forms:

Navigating a model and finding content
Querying a model to dissect its complexity and answer questions
Creating Filters and Display Rules to highlight information
Creating Views to draw attention to specific model content
Exporting model data and metadata to reuse with external tools
Viewing a model as a text document, a graph, or through the lineage explorer

Scan the table of contents below for a comprehensive list of topics and sub-topics covered in this section.

For more information or training, please contact your Solidatus representative or email support@solidatus.com.

You may also be interested in FAQs or advanced topics — browse our Learning Resources section for more content.

Title: Explore and analyse models
Link: https://docs.solidatus.com/solidatus-2026.2/models/explore-and-analyse-models
Content: Many people using Solidatus will spend their time browsing, exploring, and analysing models that have already been created and updated by others.

Models are analytical tools that help you understand the data landscapes they represent. These pages are meant to cover model functionality intended to help you get the information you need from an existing model.

Analysing a model can take several forms:

Navigating a model and finding content
Querying a model to find things that meet specific criteria
Creating Filters and Display Rules to highlight information
Creating Views to draw attention to specific content that answers questions
Exporting model data and metadata to reuse in external tools
Viewing a model as a text document, a graph, or through the lineage explorer

Scan the table of contents below for a comprehensive list of topics and sub-topics covered in this section.

For more information or training, please contact your Solidatus representative or email support@solidatus.com.

You may also be interested in FAQs from users or advanced topics — browse our Additional Resources section.
Title: Models interface
Link: https://docs.solidatus.com/solidatus-2026.2/the-user-interface/models-ui
Content: There are three areas of the Solidatus platform for working with models: the Model Browser, the Model Viewer, and the Model Overview. Use the links in the table to explore the functionality in each model-related area.

Model Browser
This is where you can find and open all models you can access or create a new model. You can also perform several useful actions including exporting and importing.
Model Viewer
This is the canvas for building, exploring, and analysing models.
Model Overview
This is where you can view model information and work with version control features involving revision history and pull requests for forks. You can also access activities, settings, and permissions.

While the Model Viewer is the main canvas for building and exploring a model, lineage and model content can be explored in other areas that have unique analytical and visual capabilities.

Area
Description
Model Overview
This provides useful information about a model, including a directory of model entities, version history, settings, and links to the other areas.
Lineage Explorer
This feature allows the user to extract a subset of entities out of a complex model, so you can analyse lineage in isolation from the clutter of other parts of a model.
Graph Explorer
The Graph Explorer gives you a visualisation of a model as an animated graph. It displays entities as nodes and transitions, parent-child links, and reference relationships as edges.
